about: The area index (refactor plan step N1, convention K15): every tracked file that is not a test file belongs to exactly one area, and no file belongs to two. An area is a slice of the product through every layer, so its globs reach the Go packages (cmd/, internal/), the API handler files, the MCP tools, the server's wire_*.go stages, frontend/src, e2e and docs. Grouping by feature is virtual: files stay where they are, and this index says which area each belongs to. Ask it with `go run ./internal/tools/areas which <path>`; internal/tools/areas/areas_test.go and frontend/src/arch/areas.test.ts check it. A new file joins an area through a glob here; add a single-file entry only where an area boundary cuts through a directory.
glob_syntax: Paths are relative to the repository root, with forward slashes. `*` and `?` match within one path segment (a leading dot included); `**/` matches any number of directories, none included; a trailing `/**` matches everything below a directory. The syntax is scripts/refactor/refactor_guard.py's glob_regex.

test_files.about: Test files need no area: Go tests, TypeScript and Node tests and specs, Python tests, the Playwright specs and their helpers under e2e/tests, and everything under a testdata/ or __snapshots__/ directory (fixtures and goldens). They are the refactor guard's TEST_FILES plus the two golden directories. A test file may still be claimed, and is then attributed to that area, but never by two areas. The test-only helper modules frontend/src/arch/** and frontend/src/test/** are not test files here: they are code someone maintains, so they have an area.

glossary.meaning: The tenant. The UI says workspace; the code, the database and the API say org. Every member has a personal workspace; company workspaces have members with the roles admin or member.
A named graph of agents and people with delegates-to, hands-off-to and reviews edges, used for delegation. The Go package and tables still say team. Area agent-suite.
A named group of people in a workspace, used to grant project access. Unrelated to crews despite the shared word team. Area tenancy-identity.

The process that claims agent runs from the API and drives a vendor CLI. The UI says runner; the code says worker. It runs on a member's machine (often through the Agent Connector), as a hosted runner, or as a cloud runner. Area runner-fleet.

The credential a runner, or a script such as the openv MCP server, authenticates with: a workspace runner key, a member's personal runner key (claims only that member's runs), or a key minted for a cloud runner lease.
A runner container the API provisions for a workspace on the local Docker daemon; at most one per workspace.
A transient runner a member leases from a pool of pre-warmed nodes for a bounded time; the node is wiped when the lease ends.
The desktop launcher that pairs a member's machine through a deep link and runs agentd and openv-mcp. Area runner-fleet.
The Model Context Protocol server that gives coding agents the openv tools, each a call to the REST API. Its core is agent-suite; each tools_<area>.go file belongs to the area its tools serve.
The token-lean outline of a whole project that coding agents read. Area agent-suite.
A write an agent in proposal mode asked to make, held until a person approves it. Area agent-suite.
One pass through the guided product-definition wizard, with its answers and the in-wizard copilot chat. Area agent-suite.
An agent-led stakeholder interview reached over a shareable link. Area agent-suite.
The project's artifact tree, table and detail panes. Area requirements-core.

In the code, the project-scoped requirements surface registered by registerSuiteRoutes (product profile, V&V, quality, parties, work items, guided sessions, interviews) and the baseline-schema file of their tables. It is not an area; each registrar belongs to its own area.
A project's work items, assigned to a person or an agent. Area requirements-core.
A note or system entry on an artifact or project, with @mentions; a note can raise a to-do. Area requirements-core.
Two memberships: of a workspace (admin or member) and of a project (viewer, reviewer, editor or owner). Both are area tenancy-identity.
Whether each requirement has a verification method and passing evidence. Area verification.
A frozen snapshot of a whole project, stored as the project export JSON. Area documents. Not the baseline schema (migration 0001: db.go and schema_*.go, area platform-http).
A project's product profile is requirements-core; a shared product is an entry in the community pool of demo products that the new-project random-product roller draws from, area community.
A link that opens a project without membership, read-only or as a reviewer; the open-source showcase lists such projects. Area community.
A workspace's plan sets its limits; enforcing them is tenancy-identity. Charging for a plan (Stripe, checkout, seats) is billing.

Decides when user-visible changes turn on for a workspace. The release a deployment runs, its notes and its feature gates are platform-http; announcing a release is events-notifications; promoting one is tooling.
A persisted record that something happened; feeds the activity log, notifications and triggered automations. Area events-notifications.

areas.name: requirements-core
areas.description: Projects and what they hold: artifacts with their refs, status and review rounds, trace links and link rules, attributes, quality rules and linting, reference parties, the product profile, notes and mentions, the board, search and duplicate detection, and the requirements module, review queue and project settings pages.

areas.name: verification
areas.description: Verification and validation: verification methods, test runs and results, coverage and gaps, the traceability matrix, change impact, and evidence bundles.

areas.name: documents
areas.description: What a project becomes as files, and the files it holds: the project export and import formats (JSON, CSV, Excel, ReqIF), the download wizard, PDF, Word and V&V reports, baselines and their comparison, project templates (with the examples/ the API image serves), and attachments, figures and their previews.

areas.name: tenancy-identity
areas.description: Who someone is and what they may reach: accounts, sign-in (password, Google and OIDC), sessions and their cookies, email verification and password reset, avatars, workspaces with their members, people-teams, invitations, logo, plan limits and deletion, project members and team grants, and the authorization checks (authz.go).

areas.name: agent-suite
areas.description: The AI agents and what they do: agent definitions, runs and their orchestration, crews and crew templates, automations (scheduled and triggered), proposals, AI providers and their sign-ins, repository connections, the guided wizard with its copilot, stakeholder interviews, the AI map, the seeded default agents, and the core of the MCP server with its guide (internal/mcp/CLAUDE.md).

areas.name: runner-fleet
areas.description: Where agent runs execute: the runner (agentd) and its worker protocol, runner keys, hosted runners and their Docker provisioning, cloud runner leases and the pool, worker status, and the Agent Connector with its pairing and download.

areas.name: events-notifications
areas.description: What happened and who hears about it: the event bus and domain events, the activity log, the SSE hub, in-app notifications with their email and web-push delivery, push subscriptions and VAPID keys, and the budget, minutes, membership and release announcements.

areas.name: community
areas.description: What members share beyond their workspace: share links and the shared project view, the open-source showcase, and the community pool of demo products with its votes, starter concepts and the random-product roller.

areas.name: billing
areas.description: Paying for a workspace: the billing service and its Stripe client, the price catalogue, checkout, seats, reconciliation, the billing endpoints and the workspace's billing tab.

areas.name: platform-http
areas.description: The server under every feature: the composition root (cmd/server's main, app, config and the core wire stages), the router, the handler deps and the HTTP plumbing (respond, errors, middleware, compression, rate limits, request log, security headers), health and meta, the database connection, baseline schema and migration ledger, env parsing, the typed server configuration (internal/config) and metrics, the wire contracts Go publishes, the release a deployment runs with its notes and feature gates, the site administrator's page, and the guides (README.md and CLAUDE.md) of cmd/server, internal/api, internal/domain and internal/persistence/postgres.

areas.name: frontend-shell
areas.description: The single-page app around the features: entry and routing (App.tsx), the API client barrel and its axios instance, state, hooks, the UI kit, navigation and project layout, theme and help, the landing page, public site and user manual, the test mock, the guides of frontend/src, frontend/src/api and e2e, the build configuration, the nginx image's runtime files and public assets, and the Playwright harness.

areas.name: tooling
areas.description: How the repository is built, checked, shipped and run: scripts/, .github/ (CI, the release and refactor workflows, templates and instructions), the Makefile, the Dockerfiles and compose files, the frontend image's Railway config, lint config, the Go module files, the refactor tools and architecture guards (internal/tools, internal/archtest, frontend/scripts, frontend/src/arch), agent configuration (.claude/, .mcp.json), the repository-level docs with the system diagram (docs/diagrams), and this index.
